requirements.text: The speedometer and odometer unit shall be an onboard device complying with all requirements of UN R39 when fitted to the N1 vehicle.
The speedometer and odometer unit shall comply with all requirements of UN R39 where more than one speedometer or odometer is fitted to the vehicle.
The speedometer dial shall not carry additional graduations or numerical values beyond those permitted by UN R39.
The speedometer display shall be located within the direct field of view of the driver and be clearly legible both day and night.
The speedometer scale shall have a range wide enough to include the maximum speed of the N1 vehicle type as stated by the manufacturer.
For the N1 vehicle, the speedometer graduation shall be 1, 2, 5 or 10 km/h.
The speedometer shall indicate numerical speed values at intervals not exceeding 20 km/h where the highest value on the display does not exceed 200 km/h.
The speedometer shall indicate numerical speed values at intervals not exceeding 30 km/h where the maximum value on the display exceeds 200 km/h.
Where the unit provides a km/h-mph selection, the speedometer shall display speed in only one of km/h or mph at any one time.
The speedometer shall permanently display the unit of the speed shown.
For a vehicle whose maximum design speed Vmax lies between 45 and 100 km/h, the speedometer shall be tested at 40 km/h and at 80 % of Vmax where that speed is at least 55 km/h.
For a vehicle whose maximum design speed Vmax lies between 100 and 150 km/h, the speedometer shall be tested at 40 km/h, 80 km/h and at 80 % of Vmax where that speed is at least 100 km/h.
The test instrumentation used for measuring true vehicle speed shall be accurate to ±0.5 %.
Where a test track is used for the speedometer test, its surface shall be flat and provide sufficient adhesion.
Where a roller dynamometer is used for the speedometer test, the roller diameter shall be at least 0.4 m.
The speed indicated by the speedometer shall not be less than the true speed of the vehicle.
At each test speed specified in paragraph 5.3.5, the speedometer shall satisfy 0 ≤ (V1 − V2) ≤ 0.1 V2 + 4 km/h between displayed speed V1 and true speed V2.
The odometer display shall be visible or accessible to the driver.
The odometer of the N1 vehicle shall display at least an integer number composed of a minimum of 6 numerals.
The odometer shall display distance in the unit corresponding to that of the predominant speedometer scale.
Where the driver can select km or miles for the odometer independently of the speedometer, the odometer shall identify the unit used.
The odometer shall not deviate by more than ±4.0 % from the true distance travelled as determined under paragraph 5.7.

Where total distance values are provided via the serial data port on the standardized data link connector, the odometer shall output values that do not deviate from the rounded total distance indicated.
The odometer shall have a resolution of total distance values and total distance indicated better than or equal to 1 km or 1 mile as appropriate.
Where an electrically detectable failure prevents the odometer from meeting the requirements of UN R39, the unit shall provide a malfunction indication to the driver.
The odometer malfunction indication shall be active when the malfunction occurs and remain active as long as the malfunction persists.
The odometer malfunction indication shall be repeated each time the ignition or vehicle master control switch is activated after being cancelled.
The odometer shall protect the total distance indicated and total distance values against manipulation.
The odometer shall implement proportionate anti-tampering mitigations including, or equivalent to, mitigation 7 of Annex 5, Part B, Table B5 of UN R155.
Where the N1 vehicle is sold in a country using imperial units, the speedometer shall also be marked in mph with graduations of 1, 2, 5 or 10 mph.
Where the speedometer is marked in mph, numerical speed values shall be indicated at intervals not exceeding 20 mph and commencing at 10 or 20 mph.
Where the N1 vehicle is sold in a country using imperial units, the odometer shall be marked in miles.
The vehicle shall carry an international approval mark in a conspicuous and easily accessible position specified on the approval form.
The approval mark shall comprise a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the approving country.
The approval mark shall show the number of this Regulation, the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle.
The approval mark shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval mark shall be placed close to or on the vehicle data plate.
For conformity of production of the N1 vehicle, the speedometer shall satisfy 0 ≤ (V1 − V2) ≤ 0.1 V2 + 6 km/h between indicated speed V1 and actual speed V2.
Where relevant for the odometer accuracy test, the reference temperature at the odometer shall be 23 ± 5 °C.
The test instrumentation used for measuring true distance travelled in the odometer test shall be accurate to ±0.5 %.
The odometer accuracy test shall be conducted at a test speed between 0 and 100 km/h.
The odometer accuracy test shall cover a distance of at least 10 km or 7 miles as indicated on the odometer.
The speedometer and odometer electronic module shall be designed and constructed so that the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, complies with UN R10.
The speedometer and odometer module, as an ESA, shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
The module shall keep broadband radiated emissions between 62 and 52 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically above 30 MHz.
The module shall keep broadband radiated emissions between 52 and 63 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically above 75 MHz.
The module shall keep broadband radiated emissions at or below 63 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
The measured broadband emission values of the module shall be below the type approval limits in dBµV/m.
The module shall keep narrowband radiated emissions between 52 and 42 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically above 30 MHz.
The module shall keep narrowband radiated emissions between 42 and 53 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically above 75 MHz.
The module shall keep narrowband radiated emissions at or below 53 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
The measured narrowband emission values of the module shall be below the type approval limits in dBµV/m.
For a 12 V system, the transient pulses emitted by the module on the supply lines shall not exceed +75 V (positive) and −100 V (negative).
The module shall withstand, over 90 % of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band below 2 GHz, test levels of 60 V/m (stripline), 75 V/m (TEM cell), 60 mA (BCI), 30 V/m (ALSE) and 21 V/m (reverberation chamber).
The module shall withstand, above 2 GHz, test levels of 10 V/m in the ALSE method and 7 V/m in the reverberation chamber method.

The module shall withstand, over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz band below 2 GHz, minimum test levels of 50 V/m (stripline), 62.5 V/m (TEM cell), 50 mA (BCI), 25 V/m (ALSE) and 18 V/m (reverberation chamber).
The module shall show no degradation of performance of its immunity related functions during the immunity tests of Annex 9.
For a 12 V system, the module shall withstand test pulse 1 at −75 V for 500 pulses at functional performance status III for both related and non-related immunity functions.
For a 12 V system, the module shall withstand test pulse 2a at +37 V for 500 pulses at FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for non-related functions.
For a 12 V system, the module shall withstand test pulse 3a at −112 V for 1 hour at FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for non-related functions.
For a 12 V system, the module shall withstand test pulse 3b at +75 V for 1 hour at FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for non-related functions.
Where the module is required to operate during engine start phases, it shall meet functional status B under the starting profile with 10 pulses.
Where the module contains no electronic oscillator operating above 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with the narrowband emission requirements of paragraph 6.6.2.
Where the module is not switched, contains no switches and includes no inductive load, it shall be deemed to comply with the transient conducted emission requirements of paragraph 6.7.
The speedometer and odometer module shall carry the approval mark described in paragraph 5.3 when it conforms to a type approved under UN R10.
The module shall carry the international approval mark in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form.
The module's approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting approval.
The module's approval mark shall show the number of this Regulation, the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle.
The module's approval marking need not be visible once the module is installed in the vehicle.
Each sample module submitted for testing shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
The dimension of the approval mark affixed to the module shall be at least 6 mm.
When the instrument cluster is in normal operating mode during the 50 km/h immunity test, unexpected warnings and inconsistent variation of the odometer shall be treated as a failure of the module.
During the immunity test the module's indicated vehicle speed shall stay within ±20 % of the 50 km/h nominal test speed.
During the broadband emission test, the module shall be operated in normal operation mode, preferably at maximum load.
The ambient noise during the module's broadband emission test shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of paragraph 6.5.2.1.
Where peak detectors are used for the module's emission measurements, a 20 dB correction factor as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.
During the immunity tests, the module shall be switched on and stimulated into its normal operating condition.
The module's immunity shall be tested over the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
In the 20 to 400 MHz range, the immunity test signal shall be amplitude modulated at 1 kHz with 80 % modulation depth.
In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz range, the immunity test signal shall use pulse modulation type 2 with 3 µs on-time and 3,333 µs period.
In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz ranges, the immunity test signal shall use pulse modulation type 3 with 500 µs on-time and 1,000 µs period.
The module's absorber chamber immunity test shall use the substitution method per ISO 11452-2 with vertical polarization.
The module's bulk current injection test shall use the substitution method with the injection probe positioned 150 mm from the module.
Test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b per ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the module's supply lines and to other connections operationally connected to supply lines.
Where the module is exclusively reserved for mounting on vehicles without a 12 V/24 V starter motor, it is not subject to the starting profile test.
The module's transient conducted emissions shall be measured per ISO 7637-2 on its supply lines and on other connections operationally connected to supply lines.

For the vehicle-level broadband emission test at 10 m antenna distance, the module's contribution shall keep the vehicle within limits E = 32 dBµV/m (30–75 MHz), E = 32 + 15.13 log(F/75) (75–400 MHz) and E = 43 dBµV/m (400–1,000 MHz).
For the vehicle-level narrowband emission test at 10 m antenna distance, the module's contribution shall keep the vehicle within 28 dBµV/m (30–230 MHz) and 35 dBµV/m (230–1,000 MHz).
For the module as an ESA, the broadband emission limit below 75 MHz shall follow E = 62 − 25.13 log(F/30) dBµV/m with a 120 kHz bandwidth.
For the module as an ESA, the narrowband emission limit below 75 MHz shall follow E = 52 − 25.13 log(F/30) dBµV/m with a 120 kHz bandwidth.
